Compress separator-grid junctions using uniform 2×2 blocks (task-f362c6ff) For ARC tasks like task-f362c6ff, sample the colors at every horizontal/vertical separator intersection, including boundary lines, to form a junction matrix. Remove only contiguous outermost rows or columns whose entries are all the separator/background color; do not trim uniform rows or columns in the interior. For each overlapping 2×2 block of the remaining matrix, output its common color if all four junctions match; otherwise output the interior tile/background color. The output has one fewer row and column than the trimmed junction matrix. Infer colors from the input and demonstrations. Validated example: junction columns c=[2,8,14,20,26] and rows r=[0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21]. After removing the top and bottom all-4 rows, 2×2 block reduction yields [[7,7,0,0],[5,7,7,7],[5,5,7,9],[7,5,7,9],[7,5,7,9]]. Directly submitting a sampled junction matrix is incorrect; perform the overlapping-block reduction. Another confirmed example used junction matrix [[6,6,8,8],[6,6,8,8]]; trimming the two rightmost all-8 columns left [[6,6]], producing [[6]]. Demonstrations also support mixed blocks taking the interior color. Validate sampling coordinates, trim only qualifying outer boundaries, and check every output block.

Additional solved test: separator rows r=[0,5,10,15,20] and columns c=[0,6,12,18,24] gave junction matrix [[3,3,3,7,7],[6,6,3,7,7],[6,6,3,3,3],[3,1,1,8,8],[3,1,1,8,8]]. This supports keeping non-uniform edge rows/columns and using the interior tile color for every mixed block.
